title: Dynamic Ultrasound Beamforming Using Left-to-Right Arithmetic Adders on FPGA
summary: Adder trees are the computational backbone of delay-and-sum (DAS) ultrasound beamforming, where their implementation directly determines the energy, throughput, and area of a real-time imaging pipeline. Conventional parallel adder trees perform full-precision combinational reduction on every sample, leading to wide critical paths, high LUT consumption, and timing failures on small FPGA devices. This paper presents an alternative adder tree architecture based on \emph{left-to-right (LR)} or \emph{most significant digit first (MSDF) arithmetic}.
